targets.claudeCode: Claude Code subagent: .claude/agents/<name>.md (Cursor and VS Code read this folder too)

rules.rule_text: Write one Markdown file: YAML frontmatter between --- markers, then the subagent's system prompt as the body.
rules.evidence: Subagent files use YAML frontmatter for configuration, followed by the system prompt in Markdown:

rules.rule_text: The opening --- must be the file's first line; otherwise the file is treated as documentation and skipped.
rules.evidence: **An opening `---` that isn't the file's first line**

rules.rule_text: Only name and description are required; a file without either is skipped.
rules.evidence: Only `name` and `description` are required.

rules.rule_text: name is a short identifier in lowercase letters and hyphens, such as code-reviewer: no colon, not starting with -, at most 256 characters.
rules.evidence: Names can't contain `:`

rules.rule_text: Use only the documented field names, spelled exactly (camelCase such as disallowedTools, permissionMode): an unknown field is ignored silently.
rules.evidence: must match the table exactly: Claude Code ignores a field it doesn't recognize without reporting an error.

rules.rule_text: The body is the subagent's whole system prompt: it does not get the main Claude Code prompt, so state its role, steps and output format in full.
rules.evidence: Subagents receive only this system prompt plus basic environment details like the working directory, not the Claude Code system prompt.

rules.rule_text: description says when to delegate to this subagent; make it specific enough to pick this one over others, and brief.
rules.evidence: Make each description specific enough to route to the right subagent

rules.rule_text: If the subagent should run without being asked, say so in the description, for example "Use proactively after code changes".
rules.evidence: To encourage proactive delegation, include phrases like "use proactively" in your subagent's description field.

rules.rule_text: Design the subagent for one specific task.
rules.evidence: each subagent should excel at one specific task

rules.rule_text: List only the tools the job needs in tools; a reviewer or researcher leaves out Edit and Write.
rules.evidence: grant only necessary permissions for security and focus

rules.rule_text: tools is a comma-separated string such as Read, Grep, Glob, Bash (or a YAML list); omitting it inherits every tool.
rules.evidence: as a comma-separated string such as `Read, Grep, Bash` or a YAML list. Inherits every tool available to subagents if omitted.

rules.rule_text: model, if set, is sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, a full model ID, or inherit; leave it out unless the task asks for a model.
rules.evidence: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full model ID such as `claude-opus-5-5`, or `inherit`

rules.rule_text: permissionMode, if set, is default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions or plan; leave it out unless the task asks for one.
rules.evidence: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, or `manual` as an alias for `default`

rules.rule_text: In the body, say exactly what to look for or do, in order, and how to format the result returned to the main conversation.
rules.evidence: a detailed prompt that specifies exactly what to look for and how to format output

rules.rule_text: A subagent cannot ask the user questions (AskUserQuestion is removed): tell it what to do when something is unclear, such as stating the assumption in its report.
rules.evidence: The first filter removes these tools, even when listed in the `tools` field:

rules.rule_text: Write one Markdown file with YAML frontmatter, then the subagent's prompt as the body.
rules.evidence: Each subagent is a markdown file with YAML frontmatter:

rules.rule_text: Frontmatter fields are name, description, model, readonly and is_background; readonly: true blocks file edits and state-changing shell commands, which suits reviewers and researchers.
rules.evidence: If `true`, the subagent runs with restricted write permissions (no file edits, no state-changing shell commands).

rules.rule_text: name uses lowercase letters and hyphens.
rules.evidence: Use lowercase letters and hyphens.

rules.rule_text: Spend the most care on description: it decides when the agent delegates to this subagent.
rules.evidence: The `description` field determines when Agent delegates to your subagent.

rules.rule_text: Name the concrete situation in the description, not a vague one like "general tasks".
rules.evidence: Be specific: "Use when implementing authentication flows with OAuth providers."

rules.rule_text: If the subagent should run without being asked, write "use proactively" or "always use for" in the description.
rules.evidence: Include phrases like "use proactively" or "always use for" in your description field to encourage automatic delegation.

rules.rule_text: Give the subagent one clear responsibility; no generic helper.
rules.evidence: Each subagent should have a single, clear responsibility. Avoid generic "helper" agents.

rules.rule_text: Keep the prompt short, specific and direct; a long prompt makes it slower, not smarter.
rules.evidence: Long, rambling prompts dilute focus. Be specific and direct.

rules.rule_text: model defaults to inherit; set a specific model ID only if the task asks for one.
rules.evidence: Uses the same model as the parent agent. This is the default.

rules.rule_text: A Codex custom agent is a TOML file, one agent per file, not Markdown.
rules.evidence: Each file defines one custom agent.

rules.rule_text: The file must define name, description and developer_instructions.
rules.evidence: Every standalone custom agent file must define:

rules.rule_text: Put the agent's prompt in developer_instructions as a TOML multi-line string between triple quotes.
rules.evidence: developer_instructions = """

rules.rule_text: name identifies the agent; match the file name to it.
rules.evidence: Codex identifies the custom agent by its `name` field.

rules.rule_text: Do not name the agent default, worker or explorer unless the task asks to replace that built-in agent.
rules.evidence: If a custom agent name matches a built-in agent such as `explorer`, your custom agent takes precedence.

rules.rule_text: Leave out sandbox_mode, approval_policy, model_provider and mcp_servers: in an agent file they do not override the parent session.
rules.evidence: Other session settings, including `sandbox_mode`, `approval_policy`,

rules.rule_text: The agent inherits the parent's permissions, so a reviewer must say "Do not edit files." in developer_instructions.
rules.evidence: They inherit the parent's

rules.rule_text: To take capabilities away, set feature keys such as features.shell_tool to false.
rules.evidence: To reduce a custom agent's capabilities, set supported feature keys to `false`:

rules.rule_text: Make the agent narrow and opinionated: one job, and instructions that keep it from drifting into adjacent work.
rules.evidence: The best custom agents are narrow and opinionated.

rules.rule_text: Codex spawns subagents when asked, so description should say what the agent is for in words a request would use.
rules.evidence: Ask for subagents or parallel agent work directly.

rules.rule_text: Repository custom agents live in .github/agents as <name>.agent.md: Markdown with YAML frontmatter, then the prompt.
rules.evidence: `.github/agents` folder

rules.rule_text: description is required: say briefly what the agent does and its domain.
rules.evidence: Write a brief `description` (required)

rules.rule_text: name is optional and defaults to the file name.
rules.evidence: If unset, the name will default to the filename

rules.rule_text: The file name may use only letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore.
rules.evidence: Note that the filename may only contain the following characters:

rules.rule_text: tools lists tool names or aliases, such as ["read", "search"]; omitting it gives every tool, so list only what the job needs.
rules.evidence: Provide a list of specific tool names or aliases

rules.rule_text: Use the aliases execute, read, edit, search, agent, web and todo; unrecognized tool names are ignored.
rules.evidence: All unrecognized tool names are ignored

rules.rule_text: The prompt below the frontmatter is at most 30,000 characters.
rules.evidence: The prompt can be a maximum of 30,000 characters.

rules.rule_text: Leave target out so the agent works in both VS Code and GitHub; set vscode or github-copilot only if the task limits it.
rules.evidence: Optionally, set the `target` property to either `vscode` or `github-copilot`

rules.rule_text: State in the prompt what the agent must not touch, as the official testing example does with production code.
rules.evidence: Focus only on test files and avoid modifying production code unless specifically requested
